source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Data Canopy's Lithia Springs campus publishes 10 MW of IT capacity and 19,500 square feet of technical space, a mid-scale footprint rather than a hyperscale one.

The operator publishes no rack count, no accelerator count, and no power density, so any conversion from megawatts to racks is an outside estimate. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 10 MW is roughly 250 racks. At 10 kW per rack, the same load is about 1,000 racks. The square footage does not settle which applies. Across 250 racks, 19,500 square feet implies about 78 square feet per rack, a plausible hall. Across 1,000 racks it implies under 20 square feet per rack, which is tight for training gear. The building is sized for real compute, but not for the densities that dominate frontier training.

The only published certification is LEED. That is a green building rating, and it says nothing about power redundancy, cooling topology, or network paths. It does not establish whether the campus can host high-density training racks, and no such specification is published.

In Georgia this campus ranks third by published megawattage among the five facilities in the state that publish a figure. Those five total 76.3 MW, so this campus is about 13 percent of the state's published capacity. The state has 49 mapped facilities, and most publish no figure at all, so the published total is a floor rather than a full accounting of Georgia's data center load. What the data does not cover is the constraint that matters most: the power available to the site, the interconnection queue, and the generation behind it. A 10 MW figure describes the building, not the grid it draws from.
